A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dimensionality-estimation study. Their main text, figures, equations, references, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial theoretical additions and removals.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and analyses of neural recordings and Llama 3 representations, including the supplementary analysis in Figure S1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original synthetic experiments and neural-recording and language-model analyses in Figures 1–4 and S1.

M1.justification: The original global and local estimators remain, but v2 adds density-ratio weighting for both stimuli and neurons, exclusion of missing-entry products, finite-population estimators for sampling without replacement, and an N-trial noise-correction extension. These change the proposed procedures beyond v1's existing sample weighting.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear and random-Fourier-feature models, neural recordings, and nine-language FLORES+/Llama 3 representations, including Appendix C. Sparse matrices and biased orientation sampling are proposed applications, not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the naive, row-corrected, and column-corrected estimators and the local TwoNN comparison. Newly cited prior bias-correction methods are discussed but not added to the empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported experimental procedures, model dimensions, subsampling settings, and local-distance construction remain unchanged. Figure 1 newly specifies fixed Q=100 and P=200 for its two panels; this documents previously unstated settings rather than establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The sample-size and local-radius sweeps and Figure S1's comparison of averaged ratios with ratios of averages are retained. The new sampling and noise discussions introduce theoretical extensions, not additional robustness experiments or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 random draws for Figure 3 and the same Appendix C iteration counts: 50, 500, 250, and 50 across the neural datasets. Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged; the N-trial proposal concerns noise correction, not experimental replication.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 3, 4, and S1 retain identical plotted content. Figure 2 retains its result curves and adds reference lines. Numerical findings and empirical conclusions remain unchanged; the new extensions have no newly reported experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: v2 adds the naive-estimator scaling law and derivations for noise correction, importance sampling, and finite-population estimation. It removes v1 Appendix B's CKA, joint-dimensionality, and excess-dimensionality derivations. Appendix A.3 also corrects the expanded t4 denominators from P(P−1)(P−3) to P(P−1)(P−2).

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about finite-sample correction, noise resistance, and local dimensionality remain. The introduction additionally advertises importance-sampling correction and sparse-matrix applicability, modestly broadening the stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive guidance on task versus neuron centering, biased sampling, correlated-noise failure conditions, and computational limitations. It interprets the new scaling law and existing estimator plateaus. v1's interpretation connecting representational alignment to joint and excess dimensionality is removed with Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit implementation link, whereas v1 only mentions supplementary code and data. It also supplies fixed sample counts in Figure 1, computational time and memory estimates, corrected implementation formulas, and vectorizable expressions for the finite-population extension.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dahmen et al. (2020), Pospisil and Pillow (2024), Mazzucato et al. (2016), and Chun et al. (2025). The introduction now contrasts earlier corrections with its claimed weaker assumptions and correction of both sampling axes; the discussion adds positioning relative to spectral-moment estimation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains. v2 reorganizes Section 3 into scaling and bias subsections, moves implementation before a grouped extensions section, adds a code-availability section, and clarifies notation and centering. These are localized structural and explanatory edits rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: All five figures are retained, with some resizing and relocation. Figure 2 adds gray reference lines and an explanatory caption; Figure 1's caption expands. Conference headers, compact affiliations, and equation layout also change, without introducing new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects implementation formulas and improves access information and explanatory guidance. However, the new finite-population formula S15 omits two-pair index contributions and fails to reproduce its target even with full observation. Appendix A.4 also asserts correlated-noise reduction without sufficient covariance assumptions. These substantive problems in the added extensions coexist with useful corrections, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
